title: Enslaved miners of Laurion and the flight from Decelea
note: Under-recorded enslaved population: over 20,000 enslaved workers escaped from Athens and the Laurion silver mines after Sparta fortified Decelea in 413 BCE (Thucydides 7.27).

title: Aspasia of Miletus in Classical Athens
note: Under-recorded women in classical antiquity: intellectual partner of Pericles, non-citizen metic woman praised by Socrates and Plato in Menexenus, mother of Pericles the Younger.

title: Enfranchisement of enslaved rowers at the Battle of Arginusae
note: Exceptional grant of freedom and Athenian citizenship to enslaved people who rowed in the Athenian fleet at Arginusae (406 BCE), attested in Aristophanes' Frogs and historical commentary.

title: Nok Culture terracotta and early iron metallurgy in West Africa
note: Coverage-gap contemporary in Sub-Saharan Africa: sophisticated terracotta sculpture and bloomery iron-smelting furnaces in central Nigeria contemporary with Classical Greece.
